question_en: A country with little or no external trade is most likely one that practices:
explanation_en: Autarky refers to a policy of seeking self-sufficiency by engaging in little or no external trade.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 16 Introduction to Geopolitics - Answers.pdf
question_en: Exogenous geopolitical risk factors are best described as those that are:
option_c: known in terms of timing but not outcome.
explanation_en: Exogenous risk refers to unanticipated geopolitical events. Thematic risk refers to factors with known or anticipated long-term effects. Event risk refers to factors that are known in terms of timing but not outcome.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 16 Introduction to Geopolitics - Answers.pdf
question_en: The primary goals of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) include:
explanation_en: The primary goals of the IMF are to promote international monetary cooperation, facilitate growth of international trade, promote exchange rate stability, assist in establishing a multilateral payment system, and provide resources to members with balance of payments difficulties. Reducing global poverty is a role of the World Bank. Resolving trade disputes is a role of the World Trade Organization.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 16 Introduction to Geopolitics - Answers.pdf
question_en: Geopolitical risks are best described as having:
option_a: broad impacts on countries or regions, rather than discrete impacts on specific companies.
option_b: impacts that are not typically captured by scenario analysis.
option_c: greater impacts during recessionary phases of business cycles.
explanation_en: Geopolitical risks often have greater impacts during recessions than they would likely have during expansions. Geopolitical risks may have discrete impacts on specific companies or industries as well as broad impacts on countries and regions. Scenario analysis is a technique for modeling the potential impacts of geopolitical risks.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 16 Introduction to Geopolitics - Answers.pdf
question_en: Black swan risk refers to exogenous geopolitical risks that have substantial:
option_a: short-term eects and a low probability of occurrence.
option_b: long-term eects and a low probability of occurrence.
option_c: long-term eects and a high probability of occurrence.
explanation_en: Exogenous risks relate to unanticipated geopolitical risk. A black swan risk is an exogenous risk with a low likelihood of occurrence, but a high short-term impact.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 16 Introduction to Geopolitics - Answers.pdf
question_en: A geopolitical risk that will have the biggest impact in the environmental, social, and governance realm will most likely have a velocity classification that is:
explanation_en: A low-velocity classification describes a geopolitical risk that will take a long time to impact investment values. Risks that land in the environmental, social, and governance area tend to be low-velocity risks.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 16 Introduction to Geopolitics - Answers.pdf
question_en: A country joins a free trade agreement with its surrounding countries. The country also enacts a law prohibiting its domestic manufacturers from exporting military technology. In terms of geopolitics, which of these actions is considered cooperative?
explanation_en: In the context of geopolitics, "cooperation" refers to interaction and engagement among countries. While participating in trade agreements is considered cooperative, banning exports of a particular good is considered non-cooperative.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 16 Introduction to Geopolitics - Answers.pdf
question_en: With respect to analyzing geopolitical risk, velocity most likely refers to the speed with which:
option_b: mitigation strategies can be put into place.
option_c: investment values reect the eects of a risk.
explanation_en: The effects of geopolitical risk on investments can be analyzed in terms of likelihood (probability of occurrence), impact (magnitude of the effects on investment outcomes), and velocity (speed with which investment values reflect these effects).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: Two countries trade freely with each other and have agreed to specific tariffs on imports from other countries. The workers in either country may freely cross the common border to work in the other country. The two countries have agreed to common economic policies, but they use separate currencies. This type of cooperation is best described as a(n):
explanation_en: The two countries are a part of an economic union. In an economic union, there is (1) free trade among members, (2) common restrictions (tariffs) on imports from non-members, (3) free movement of production factors (labor), and (4) common economic institutions and coordination of economic policies. While a customs union has common tariffs on imports from non-union countries and free trade, it does not allow workers to cross the borders freely and does not have common economic institutions. A monetary union requires all of the listed items and a common currency.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the items below is NOT a valid reason why nations adopt trade restrictions? To:
option_a: protect industries in which they have a comparative advantage.
option_b: prohibit foreign firms from increasing market share by selling products below cost.
option_c: protect industries that are highly sensitive to national security.
explanation_en: If a particular country enjoys a comparative advantage in a particular industry, no protection is needed.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: Country P begins importing goods from Country Q. In the long run, benefits from this trade relationship will most likely accrue to:
option_c: both Country P and Country Q.
explanation_en: Both countries in an international trade relationship benefit in the long run. Costs of international trade tend to be short-run effects in specific domestic industries.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: In the context of international trading blocs, the primary feature of an economic union that distinguishes it from a common market is the adoption of a common:
option_c: set of trade restrictions with non-members.
explanation_en: An economic union is a common market that has also adopted common institutions and economic policy. Both common markets and economic unions adopt a common set of trade restrictions with non-members. Neither requires the adoption of a common currency, which is a characteristic of a monetary union.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements about the costs and benefits of international trade is most accurate?
option_a: Increased international trade benefits all groups in the trading countries.
option_b: The costs of trade are greater than the benefits with regard to domestic employment.
option_c: The costs of trade primarily affect those in domestic industries that compete with imports.
explanation_en: The benefits of trade are greater than the costs for the overall economy, but those in domestic industries competing with imports may suffer costs in the form of reduced profits or employment.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: If a country imposes a tariff on an imported good, which groups will most likely be harmed by the tariff?
explanation_en: Domestic consumers in the country that imposes a tariff are harmed because they must pay higher prices for the good. Tariffs benefit domestic producers of the good by effectively imposing a price increase on competing imports. A tariff does not affect foreign consumers of the good.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following lists of trading blocs is most accurately ordered by degree of economic integration, from least to most integrated?
option_a: Free trade area, economic union, common market.
option_b: Customs union, economic union, monetary union.
option_c: Free trade area, common market, customs union.
explanation_en: The order by degree of economic integration (from least to most integrated) is as follows: free trade areas, customs union, common market, economic union, and monetary union.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: The most integrated type of trading bloc or regional trade agreement is a(n):
explanation_en: A monetary union, such as the Euro zone, is the most integrated type of trading bloc or regional trade agreement because the members adopt a common currency.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: Who benefits least from tariffs?
explanation_en: A tax imposed on imports is called a tariff, which benefits domestic producers and domestic governments. Domestic consumers lose through higher prices, less choice of products, and lower quality products.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which form of regional trading agreement is least likely to allow free movement of labor?
explanation_en: Economic unions and common markets remove all barriers to the movement of labor and capital among their members. Customs unions do not have this feature.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: David Forsythe and Linda Novak are discussing the advantages and disadvantages of import restrictions. They state the following: Forsythe: One of the groups that benefits from import restrictions is often the government that imposes them. Novak: Import restrictions impose costs on specific groups, such as the country's import industries, but these costs are more than offset by the benefits to other groups and to the economy as a whole. With respect to these statements:
explanation_en: Forsythe is correct. A primary reason why trade restrictions remain widespread is the revenue that governments receive from tariffs. Novak is incorrect. Trade restrictions benefit specific groups, such as workers in the protected industries, but those benefits are most often less than the costs imposed on consumers and other industries as a whole.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Economics\Reading 17 International Trade - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which group is most likely to benefit from a quota imposed on imports of a good?
explanation_en: Quotas restrict the supply of imported goods, which increases the price domestically, benefiting domestic producers but harming domestic consumers. While some specific foreign producers may also benefit from the higher prices created by the quota if they receive the revenue transfer (due to higher prices received for all goods sold under the import license), foreign producers as a whole are likely to experience decreased sales in the country that imposes a quota.
